typed_core.name: awarding_agency_or_insurer
typed_core.why: disambiguator — SSA vs VA vs private insurer changes interpretation
typed_core.prompt_hint: The paying agency matters: SSA (SSDI/SSI), VA (service-connected disability), or a private disability insurer — extract verbatim

typed_core.name: claim_or_account_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII — attaches the award to the borrower

typed_core.name: benefit_program_or_policy
typed_core.why: disambiguator — SSDI vs SSI vs LTD policy; affects continuance/gross-up

typed_core.name: award_letter_date
typed_core.why: identity — when the award was stated

typed_core.name: payment_frequency
typed_core.why: disambiguator for the amount — monthly vs annual

typed_core.name: taxable_status
typed_core.why: processor — non-taxable benefit income may be grossed up
typed_core.prompt_hint: Non-taxable disability income is commonly grossed up in underwriting — capture taxable_status and the gross figure exactly

typed_core.name: continuation_or_permanency_statement
typed_core.why: processor — is income likely to continue (the key qualifying question)

typed_core.name: retroactive_or_lump_sum_amount
typed_core.why: processor — a lump sum may appear as a large deposit/asset
typed_core.prompt_hint: A retroactive/back-pay lump sum is distinct from the recurring monthly benefit — do not add them

typed_core.name: appeal_or_pending_review_status
typed_core.why: processor — a pending appeal undermines income stability

nested_lists.name: deductions_or_offsets
nested_lists.shape_reason: offsets (e.g. Medicare premium, workers-comp offset) reconcile gross to net; few items, flat is cheap

fields.name: label
fields.why: the offset/deduction label (e.g. Medicare premium, workers-comp offset)

fields.name: amount
fields.why: the offset amount reconciling gross to net

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance snippet for the offset row

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: agency-issued, not executed by the borrower

rejected.name: cost_of_living_adjustment
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL free text; no consumer -> catch-all

encoding_variations: Benefit amount is stated monthly or annually; payment_frequency beside it prevents a 12x error
Taxability is stated as prose ('this benefit is not subject to federal income tax'), a checkbox, or omitted — keep taxable_status verbatim; absence != taxable
Continuance appears as an explicit review date, 'permanent', or 'subject to periodic review' — keep both benefit_end_or_review_date and the free-text continuation_or_permanency_statement

open_questions.recommendation: flat-row — needed to explain the gross-to-net gap for gross-up GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Gross vs net for qualifying. Both are captured; underwriting may use gross (grossed up) or net depending on program.
open_questions.recommendation: keep both; a future income rule chooses

open_questions.q: Continuance as structured vs prose. The 3-year continuance decision hinges on this.
open_questions.recommendation: keep prose now; tags/rules judge continuance — a schema field should not GEET'S DECISION (LP-439): keep continuance as prose — tags/rules judge continuance, a schema field should not.

notes: No rules consume this type today, so there is no rule floor; every field earns its place on identity, PII, processor use, or disambiguation.
beneficiary_name is standard-sensitivity; kept as a typed field for identity but not promoted to _PII_FIELDS (registry is for SSN/account/EIN class).
claim_or_account_number_masked needs _PII_FIELDS registration (pre_masked true); not currently in the 7-field registry.
